name: Millenary Benedictine Abbey of Pannonhalma and its Natural Environment
description: Pannonhalma Archabbey crowns a 282-metre hill in western Hungary, where Benedictine monks have lived since 996. Its buildings span a thousand years of styles, from a 13th-century basilica and crypt to a Baroque refectory with trompe-l'œil painting and a library of about 400,000 volumes. Around 50 monks still live here, and a school runs alongside them.
